name: Permutation Cycle
description: For a permutation P [1... N ] of integers from 1 to N , function f is defined as follows: Let g ( i ) be the minimum positive integer j such that f ( i , j ) = i . We can show such j always exists. For given N , A , B , find a permutation P of integers from 1 to N such that for 1 ≤ i ≤ N , g ( i ) equals either A or B .
input_specification: The only line contains three integers N , A , B ( 1 ≤ N ≤ 10 6 , 1 ≤ A , B ≤ N ).
output_specification: If no such permutation exists, output -1 . Otherwise, output a permutation of integers from 1 to N .
approach_summary: Uncover mathematical invariant or parity constraint. Construct the solution step-by-step maintaining the validity condition without exhaustive search.
